result.summary: Validates block index records and file metadata in BlockManager during node initialization. It rejects block index entries with missing or mismatched parent links and fails loading if the database reports a negative last-block-file number or an arbitrary file number lacking stored file info.
result.problem: Corrupted records in the LevelDB block index database can crash node initialization or cause undefined behavior. A negative last-block-file number causes an out-of-bounds vector read, while an entry with a null or height-mismatched parent pointer triggers an assertion failure in CBlockIndex::GetAncestor rather than failing cleanly with a reindex prompt.
evidence: PR description and commit: "A last block file number of -1 makes it read before the start of a vector. A very large one makes it allocate and read that many file infos. A block without a parent, or with a parent at the wrong height, hits the assert in CBlockIndex::GetAncestor."
Unit tests in src/test/validation_chainstatemanager_tests.cpp inject corrupt database entries and verify LoadBlockIndex fails cleanly.
result.changed_since_previous: Diff provided for the first time (previously nopatch); implementation matches the earlier summary.
result.card: Validates block index entries and file metadata during node initialization to catch database corruption early. Corrupted LevelDB entries in blocks/index could cause out-of-bounds reads from negative file numbers or assertion failures in CBlockIndex::GetAncestor from missing or invalid parent links, rather than cleanly prompting the user to reindex. The change rejects inconsistent parent pointers and invalid last-block-file numbers during block index loading, accompanied by unit tests reproducing each corrupt state.

risk.why: Flawed block index validation logic during initialization could prevent valid nodes or unusual chain configurations from starting up.
